title: Major depression: episode, severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's depressive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for mood.

HPI: Pt is a 77 y/o female presenting for scheduled follow-up of major depressive disorder, recurrent. Pt reports stable mood over the past 3 months. Denies any episodes of low mood, anhedonia, or sleep disturbances. States she feels "back to her old self" and is enjoying hobbies again. No reports of weight changes or fatigue. Pt reports good compliance with current regimen.

Medication List:
- Sertraline 50mg PO QD
- Multivitamin PO QD

Review of Systems:
General: No fatigue, no weight changes.
Psychiatric: No depressed mood, no sleep issues.
Neurological: No tremors, no gait changes.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History: Pt lives with her spouse. Retired. Enjoys gardening and walking. No tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History: Mother had hypertension. Father had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals:
BP: 128/82
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Ht: 124 lbs

Recent Labs:
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/L
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
Glucose: 105 mg/dL

Exam:
Gen: Alert and oriented x3. Well-groomed.
Psych: Cooperative. Normal speech and tone. Affect is bright and congruent. Mood is stable. Thought process is linear and goal-directed. Insight and judgment are intact.
Physical: CTAB. RRR. Lungs clear.

Assessment:
1. Major depressive disorder, recurrent. Pt is currently in full remission.

Plan:
1. Continue current dose of Sertraline.
2. Continue to monitor mood and side effects.
3. Return to clinic in 3 months for routine follow-up.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 05/12/2026
explanations: Major depressive disorder, recurrent, in full remission (no HCC): F33.42.

distractors.why: The provider documents full remission: code the remission, not an active severity.
The remission is full, not partial.
